motivation: Test whether a faster plant-condition dimension temporally leads a slower within-meadow occupancy dimension, rather than merely covarying with it.
ecological_hypothesis: Lower source-year Thalassia shoot density precedes lower next-year within-transect focal frequency after current frequency/abundance and persistent site identity are already known.

primary_model.row_eligibility: source-year shoot_density_mean_m2 nonmissing; consecutive target year exists
primary_model.split: strict walk-forward by target year; train only earlier target years

support_rule.direction_audit: standardized source_condition coefficient must be positive in >=60% of scored target years and have positive median coefficient

secondary_blade_length.design: same target, learner, walk-forward split and support rule on blade-length-eligible rows; log blade measurement count replaces log shoot measurement count
secondary_blade_length.role: sensitivity/biological replication only; cannot rescue a null or adverse shoot-density primary result

interpretation_map.supported: Consistent with an annual density-to-occupancy cascade: plant-density condition contains leading information about future within-meadow thinning beyond current focal occupancy/abundance and stable site identity.
interpretation_map.unsupported: No robust evidence that shoot density is an annual leading indicator of future focal-frequency decline under this design; state dimensions can still differ in temporal lability without forming a simple cascade.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc ecological hypothesis generated after the state-hierarchy result; not independent confirmation.
Predictive lead does not establish shoot density as a causal driver of frequency decline.
Shared local stress, residual meadow quality, and measurement processes can produce the same lagged association.
Do not retune target years, alpha, baseline covariates, condition transformation, support rule, or replace the primary with blade length after opening the result.
A positive result supports temporal ordering at annual resolution, not a universal degradation sequence.
